rows.en: It was a bolt from the blue.

ghs.en: It was a bolt out of the blue.

rows.jp: 桜庭と再会したのは、一年生の頃だ。
rows.en: I met Sakuraba again in our first year.

ghs.en: I was a high school freshman when I was reunited with Sakuraba.

ghs.assessment: The direct object construction is ungrammatical in this context; the Japanese simply asks whether Taichi remembers him.

rows.en: “From the play at the school festival.”

rows.jp: 『苗字で呼ばれるのは好きじゃない。ヒロって呼んでくれ』
rows.en: “I don’t like being called by my last name. Call me Hiro.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I don't like being called by my last name. Please call me Hiro."

rows.jp: その顔には確かに見覚えがあった。

ghs.en: There was certainly something familiar in that face,

rows.jp: 嫌な記憶が添付されてはいたが。
rows.en: Unfortunately, it came with an unpleasant memory attached.

ghs.en: but with bad memories attached to it.
Taichi: "I wouldn't not mind, wouldn't I?"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese emphatically says that of course he minds. The stacked negation and tag question make the English logical force unstable.

highlights.text: I wouldn't not mind, wouldn't I?

rows.en: “Keep your apology. Stay away from me.”

rows.jp: 『許すか。二度と話しかけるな』

ghs.en: Taichi: "Forgive you? Never get close or talk to me again!"

rows.en: “Anyway, yesterday I saw this thing online—”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "By the way, on the 'net yesterday---』
ghs.assessment: The English dialogue closes with a Japanese corner bracket instead of the quotation mark used by the translation's own presentation format.

rows.jp: めげない。懲りない。くじけない。
rows.en: He never got discouraged. Never learned his lesson. Never gave up.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he never learns his lesson or is incorrigible. 'Unlearning' means losing previously acquired knowledge.

rows.jp: 桜庭とはそんなヤツらしい。

ghs.en: That's the kind of guy Sakuraba seemed to be.

rows.en: “I told you not to talk to me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I told you to stay away and don't talk to me!"

rows.jp: 『聞こえないのか、おまえの耳は』

ghs.en: Taichi: "Can't you hear with those ears of yours or something?"

rows.jp: 『ああ、聞こえない。片方だけな』

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Ah, I can't hear. Just on one side."

rows.jp: 『おまえにいいのをもらったときにな』
rows.en: “Since you gave it such a good shot.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "It's from when I got a nice thing from you."

rows.jp: が、自分の貞操を守っただけだ。
rows.en: But only to defend my chastity.

ghs.en: but it was just to defend my chastity.

rows.jp: 『……だからどうした。正当防衛だ』

ghs.en: Taichi: "...and so what. It was legitimate self-defense."

rows.en: “Looking back... I think I was overcome.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I think... that I was emotionally moved."

rows.jp: 『舞台のおまえは、きれいだったからな』
rows.en: “You were beautiful up on that stage.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Because you were so beautiful on that stage."

rows.jp: 『あーそうかい。あんがとな。嬉しくないけどな』
rows.en: “Oh, is that so? Thanks. Doesn't make me happy.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh so it was. Thanks. Doesn't make me happy though."

rows.jp: 『安心しろ。オレの中に、もう不純なものはない』
rows.en: “Don’t worry. There’s nothing impure left in me now.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Be at ease. There is nothing impure anymore inside of me."

ghs.assessment: The Japanese expresses skepticism about Sakuraba's claim: 'Who knows' or 'I doubt it.' The English instead questions the noun 'nothing.'

rows.jp: 『ないんだ。もう。いろいろとショックだったんだな』
rows.en: “There isn't. Not anymore. The whole thing shocked it out of me.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Nothing. No more. There were all kinds of shocks."

rows.jp: 『オレの中から、制御できない生々しいものが消えたような感じなんだ』
rows.en: “It's like all that raw, uncontrollable stuff inside me disappeared.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Feels like all the incontrollable impure things have vanished from inside me."

rows.jp: 『そりゃおまえがインポ野郎ってことだ』

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sooo yer some impotent son of a bitch, right."
And he even had the guts to laugh.

rows.jp: 『ここしばらく、いなくなってくれてせいせいしてたんだが』
rows.en: “I was enjoying the peace and quiet while you were gone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And I went and felt all relieved that you had gone and disappeared for a while."

rows.jp: 『アンモナイトかと思ったら、カブトの幼虫だった』
rows.en: “I thought I’d found an ammonite. It was a beetle larva.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I was thinking it was ammonite, but it was a beetle larva."

rows.jp: 昼飯にあぶれた日があった。
rows.en: There was a day when I missed lunch.

ghs.en: There was one day when I failed to get lunch,

rows.jp: 食券もパンも売り切れていた。
rows.en: Both meal tickets and bread had sold out.

ghs.en: meal tickets and bread both sold out.

rows.jp: 山のような、購買のパン。
rows.en: A mountain of buns from the school store.

ghs.en: Procured bread, and a mountain of it.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese identifies a mountain of bread from the school store. The English mistakes the store noun for a participle meaning obtained.
ghs.remedy: A mountain of bread from the school store

rows.en: “I'm going to find the best one.”

ghs.assessment: The superlative noun phrase lacks the required determiner.
ghs.remedy: looking for the most delicious one

ghs.assessment: Taichi tells him to do as he likes and leave Taichi out of it. The English invents an objection to bringing items.
ghs.remedy: Do whatever you want on your own.

rows.jp: 『一人だと食いきれないからな』
rows.en: “I can’t finish all this by myself.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "There's too many to eat alone."

rows.jp: 『おい、このカレーパン、信じられないうまさだぞ？』
rows.en: “Hey, this curry bun is insanely good.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Hoy, this curry bread's so good that you wouldn't believe ya know?"

rows.jp: 『こっちのカツサンドは駄目だな。やる』
rows.en: “This pork cutlet sandwich is terrible. Here.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "These pork cutlet sandwiches are worthless. Have 'em."

rows.jp: 『そうか？　舌がおかしいんじゃないか？』
rows.en: “Really? Must be something wrong with your tongue.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "It is? Isn't your taste a bit strange?"

rows.jp: 群青のカリキュラムは、拘束時間が長い。
rows.en: Gunjo's curriculum kept students on campus for long hours.

ghs.en: The actual school hours are long in the curriculum of Gunjou.

rows.jp: 授業が終わっても三十分は正門も開かない。
rows.en: Even when classes ended, the front gate stayed locked another thirty minutes.

ghs.en: The lessons may be over, but the front gate won't open for thirty more minutes.

rows.jp: 門の前で待機する三十分は、いつも退屈な時間だった。
rows.en: Those thirty minutes waiting at the gate were always dull.

ghs.en: Those thirty minutes of wait in front of the gate were always a time of boredom.
He lines up next to me.

rows.jp: 『鳥はいい。次に生まれ変わる時は、鳥になる』
rows.en: “Birds have it good. Next time I'm reincarnated, I'll be a bird.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Birds are nice. Next time I'm born again, I'll be a bird."

rows.en: He said it out of nowhere.

ghs.en: That's what he said, all of a sudden.

rows.jp: 『頭はすでにどっか飛んでるみたいだけどな』

ghs.en: Taichi: "Your head looks like it's already flying in the sky though."
ghs.assessment: Taichi jokes that Sakuraba's mind has already flown off somewhere—that he is already scatterbrained. The literal flying head misses the idiom.
ghs.remedy: Looks like your mind has already flown the coop.

highlights.text: Your head looks like it's already flying in the sky

ghs.en: I became a member of the Broadcast Club.

rows.jp: 最初に部室に顔を出した日。
rows.en: The first day I showed my face in the clubroom—

ghs.en: And the very first day I showed face in the club room,

ghs.assessment: Sakuraba proposes hanging out or teaming up. The English substitutes sexual or animal mating and introduces a malformed hyphenation.
ghs.remedy: Looks like we can hang out.

rows.en: “I have no desire to hang out with you.”

rows.jp: ちなみに友貴は少し遅れてやってきた。

ghs.en: As for Tomoki, he came in a little bit later.

rows.jp: みみ先輩は、スカウトさんだったらしい。
rows.en: Apparently Mimi was the one who'd recruited him.

ghs.en: Mimi-senpai seemed to have been the scout.

rows.jp: 『島友貴っつーんだけど……よろしく』
rows.en: “I’m Tomoki Shima... Nice to meet you.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Shima Tomoki's who I am so... nice to meet you."

rows.jp: 『オレは桜庭浩。苗字で呼ばれるのは好きじゃない。ヒロって呼んでくれ』
rows.en: “I’m Hiroshi Sakuraba. I don’t like being called by my last name. Call me Hiro.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I'm Sakuraba Hiroshi. I don't like being called by my last name. Please call me Hiro."

rows.jp: 見事に及び腰にさせた。
rows.en: With one sentence, he'd put Tomoki on the defensive.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Sakuraba successfully made Tomoki hesitant or wary. The English suggests physically knocking him off balance.
ghs.remedy: He did a splendid job of putting Tomoki on guard.

rows.jp: 三人は部室で、規定時間を過ごす。
rows.en: The three of us served our required time in the clubroom.

ghs.en: The three of us spent our prescribed hours in the club room.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says spending the prescribed time there is the rule. A habit is customary behavior, not an imposed rule.

rows.jp: 『だから、そうじゃないって……どうしてわざと間違えるんだ』
rows.en: “No, that's not right... Why do you keep getting it wrong on purpose?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Told ya, it is not like that... why'd you keep making that error on purpose!"
Sakuraba: "'Cause it looks more interesting this way."
Tomoki: "Shogi is a contest you know!"

rows.jp: 『オレはやって面白いことをする』
rows.en: “I do whatever makes playing more fun.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "The stuff I do gotta be interesting."

rows.jp: 『おい、太一もどうだ？　やろうぜ』

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Hoy, Taichi, how about it? Come play."
I went and shrugged my shoulders.
Tomoki: "...he gives me the creeps, that Kurosu."

rows.jp: 俺には、小声の会話だって聞こえる。

ghs.en: Even that whispered conversation was audible to me.
that's what I wanted to shout.

rows.jp: 『……やる義理はないと思うけどな』
rows.en: “...I don't think I owe you that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I thought I didn't really have to do it though."
Tomoki: "You did have to, because you're a club member."

rows.jp: 侮蔑を込めて言うと、島友貴は顔を瞬時に紅潮させた。
rows.en: I put enough contempt into it to make Tomoki Shima flush scarlet.

ghs.en: At those words loaded with scorn, Tomoki's face for an instant turned crimson red.

rows.jp: とっくみあいになった。

ghs.en: a grappling as if trying to decide who was rider and who was horse.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simply says the narrator straddles or mounts Tomoki during the scuffle. The English invents a contest over metaphorical rider and horse roles.

highlights.text: a grappling as if trying to decide who was rider and who was horse

rows.jp: 怪我はしない程度に、苦痛のある方法で殴った。
rows.en: I hit him in ways that hurt without injuring him.

ghs.en: I beat him with technique, enough that there's pain, but not enough that there's injuries.

rows.jp: 殴りながら、俺は退屈だった。
rows.en: I was bored even as I punched him.

ghs.en: And while beating him, I was bored.

rows.jp: くだらない三文芝居に、うんざりしていた。
rows.en: Fed up with this cheap melodrama.

ghs.en: It was a worthless two-bit play, just tedious.

rows.jp: 『どうした、気の済むまでやったらいい。もっと青春度がアップするぞ』
rows.en: “What's wrong? Keep going till you're satisfied. It'll make this even more youthful.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "What is it now, best you do it as long as you feel like it. Make the level of adolescence increase more!"
Taichi: "...I quit. This is just ridiculous."

rows.jp: 『……そうだよ。最初からそうしてくれれば』
rows.en: “...Good. You could have done that from the start.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...right you will. Ya should've done it in the first place."

rows.jp: 『わかんねーんだよ。こんなの。知らねーんだから』
rows.en: “I don't know how. Nobody taught me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don'get it yannow, all this stuff 'ere. I just don't know 's all."

rows.jp: 当然であるかのようにヤツは言う。
rows.en: He said it as though it were obvious.

ghs.en: So this guy said, as if it was just a matter of course.

rows.jp: 痛みに顔をしかめて、でも友貴は恨み言は言わなかった。
rows.en: Tomoki winced at the pain but didn't complain.

ghs.en: His face was scrunched up with pain, yet Tomoki didn't have one word of complaint.

ghs.assessment: Taichi gives Sakuraba the imperative 'Work.' The English instead has Taichi promise that he himself will work.

rows.jp: もう手伝ったら、同じだからな……。
rows.en: Once I'd helped, we were all in it together...

ghs.en: I might as well help, it's all the same after all...

rows.jp: 『どうした、またスクープでもされたか』
rows.en: “What, did someone get another scoop on you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What, yet another scoop on you?"

rows.jp: 『車に轢かれて猫が死んでた。あれはよくない。よくないよな』
rows.en: “A cat got run over. It was dead. That's not right. It's not right, is it?”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "A cat got struck by a car and died. That's not good. Not good at all."

rows.jp: 『……轢かれてって……おい……どうして泣いてるんだ？』
rows.en: “Run over...? Hey... why are you crying?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...ran over then... hoy... why are you crying?"

rows.jp: 『……わからん。たぶん猫のせいだ』

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...I dunno. Maybe because of the cat."

rows.jp: 意外とナイーブだったりするらしい。
rows.en: Apparently he had a surprisingly sensitive side.

ghs.en: Surprisingly, he seems to be sort of naive.
ghs.assessment: Here ナイーブ describes Sakuraba as unexpectedly sensitive or emotionally delicate. 'Naive' instead means inexperienced or credulous.

rows.jp: ただし桜庭独自の基準で。
rows.en: Though only by Sakuraba's own standards.

ghs.en: But it's still within Sakuraba's peculiar standards.

rows.jp: 『オレは、この学校のみんなから笑いものにされているようだ』
rows.en: “Seems like everyone at this school is laughing at me.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "I seem to have been made the laughingstock of the people of this school."
I give him a detailed explanation with flowing eloquence.
ghs.assessment: The narrator carefully enunciates a short admonition so Sakuraba will understand. The English adds both a detailed explanation and rhetorical eloquence.
ghs.remedy: I spell it out with perfect enunciation.

highlights.text: a detailed explanation with flowing eloquence

rows.en: “You should've figured that out ages ago.”

rows.jp: 『……オレは、そんな滑稽な男なのか？』
rows.en: “...Am I truly such a ridiculous man?”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "...do I even look like that humorous a man?"
ghs.assessment: Sakuraba asks whether he is such a ridiculous or laughable man. 'Humorous' positively describes someone amusing and weakens the humiliation.

rows.jp: こいつはもしかして、悪意に鈍感なのかも知れない。
rows.en: Could he simply be oblivious to malice?

ghs.en: This guy might just be completely unaffected by malice, I just don't know.

rows.jp: なにかの拍子で潰れてしまうんじゃないか？
rows.en: Would something trivial crush him someday?

ghs.en: Some occasion or another comes and he'll just get destroyed, won't he?

rows.en: That was what I thought then.

ghs.en: I thought so at that time.

rows.jp: けど実際は……正反対だった。
rows.en: But the truth was... the exact opposite.

ghs.en: But the truth was... the exact opposite.

rows.jp: 桜庭は凹むわりにはタフネスで、どんな精神的惨敗からも必ず蘇生してみせた。
rows.en: For all the dents he took, Sakuraba was tough. He resurrected after every crushing emotional defeat.

ghs.en: Sakuraba may cave in and become depressed, but he had toughness so that he would experience certain resuscitation out of whatever crushing emotional defeat he suffered.

rows.jp: ひとしきり傷つくと、癒すために無茶をした。
rows.en: After he'd spent a while hurting, he'd do something reckless to heal.

ghs.en: He'd be hurt for a while, then he'd do something nonsensical to cure himself.

rows.jp: 旅立ったり、踊ったり、演奏したり。
rows.en: Go on a trip. Dance. Play music.

ghs.en: He'd set off on some journey, or he'd dance, or he'd do a musical performance.

rows.jp: 一週間くらいで、たいがい復活した。
rows.en: Usually, he was back on his feet within a week.

ghs.en: Within about a week he'd be mostly revived.

rows.jp: そして俺たちは、なんとなくつるむようになった。
rows.en: And somehow, we started hanging out.

ghs.en: And then we, someway or another, began our mate-ing.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says they gradually began hanging out together. The English turns ordinary companionship into sexual or animal mating and uses malformed hyphenation.

rows.jp: 桃園の誓いは、そのしばらく後の出来事になる―――
rows.en: Our Oath of the Peach Garden came a little later—

ghs.en: And our Oath of the Peach Garden happened not long after that---
